business_ops.seasonality: Our business is not seasonal in nature. (MD&A - 'Seasonality/Cyclicality of Business', PDF p.380). The DRHP gives no further seasonality or cyclicality discussion.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light service model with no manufacturing and no backward or forward integration disclosed. The DRHP states affirmatively that 'Our Company is not in the business of manufacturing and therefore, the Company has not undertaken any steps for capacity/facility creation' (PDF p.255), and that 'We do not own any immovable property' - the Registered Office, Corporate Office and all 136 India centres operate from leased or rented premises, or from premises provided by Licensed Professionals and partner schools, on lease tenures of 11 months to 3 years (Our Business - Properties, PDF p.241). Upstream inputs are limited to centre fit-outs (interior, electrical, furniture, branding), initial inventory of therapy material and technology hardware (printers, laptops), all procured against quotations from third-party contractors and vendors and certified by an Independent Architect (Objects of the Issue, PDF p.117-118); immovable fit-out capex is approximately 30-37% of total centre capex for Company Learning Centres and partnership centres and under 9% for School Collaboration Centres, and is not recoverable if a lease ends (Risk Factor 1). Forward reach is through owned centre formats plus revenue-share partnerships with Licensed Professionals (who provide premises and referrals) and with schools, complemented by e-therapy delivered digitally and home-delivered learning kits built on an in-house library of 2,000+ teaching tools developed by a seven-person R&D team. The Company also runs an in-house Upskilling Academy for clinician training and a Centre for Excellence and Research. market_position.basis: EXPLICIT NIL PEER SET (issuer-stated, not an extraction gap). The RHP affirmatively states four separate times that no listed comparable exists. Basis for the Offer Price, section III 'Industry Peer Group P/E ratio' (PDF p.142 / printed p.138) and section VI 'Comparison of Accounting Ratios with listed industry peers' (PDF p.143 / printed p.139) both read verbatim: 'There are no listed companies in India or other foreign jurisdictions whose business portfolio is comparable with that of our business and comparable to our scale of operations. Hence, it is not possible to provide an industry comparison in relation to our Company.' The identical sentence is repeated at section IX 'Comparison of our key performance indicators with listed industry peers' (PDF p.146). Risk Factor 24, 'Absence of Listed Industry Peers may affect investor benchmarking and valuation' (PDF p.48), states: 'There are currently no listed companies in India engaged in a business directly comparable to ours, which makes it difficult for investors to benchmark our performance against industry peers (Source: CARE Report, on page 67).' Consequently the Basis for Offer Price chapter prints NO peer-comparison table at all - there is no row of P/E, RoNW, NAV per share, Face value or Total income for any peer anywhere in the document, and peers_drhp is therefore an issuer-declared empty set rather than a missing extraction. POSITIONING BASIS: the CARE Report (commissioned and paid for by the Company) states that, based on number of centres as of March 31, 2026, the Company ranks first (1st) in India in offering intervention plans for children with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) and seventh (7th) globally among listed players operating in a similar behavioural health domain (Source: CARE Report, page 64), and that it is 'India's largest For-Profit Social Enterprise offering intervention plans for children with NDDs'. No market share percentage is printed anywhere in the RHP for the Company or for any competitor; share_pct is null because it could only be reached by deriving one, which is not permitted. The Company self-describes a value/affordability posture ('substantial value at affordable price points', 'build on our value leadership', 'accessibility, affordability, and quality of care'), but the enum value recorded is 'niche' because the defining, repeatedly stated fact is that it operates in a specialised NDD-intervention domain with no comparable listed operator in India or any foreign jurisdiction. Scale as printed: 136 centres in India (42 Tier 1, 77 Tier 2, 17 Tier 3) across 57 cities in 20 states and union territories, plus 3 acquired overseas centres in Virginia, USA, under the brand 'Mom's Belief'; over 58,000 children served since 2018; 9,205, 8,585 and 9,344 children served in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively. All industry and ranking data in this section is attributed by the RHP to the CARE Report ('Report on Neuro-developmental Disorders', July 2026, CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited), which Risk Factor 53 notes was commissioned and paid for by the Company solely for the purposes of the Issue.

opportunities: Continued network expansion with cost efficiencies: the Company intends to utilise Rs 413.61 million of the Net Proceeds to set up 319 new centres between Fiscal 2027 and Fiscal 2029, targeting underserved Tier 2 and Tier 3 communities, supported by a 33-employee business development team.

Inorganic and international expansion: acquisition on June 23, 2025 of Mom's Belief US, Inc. (wholly owned Subsidiary) and Allergy and Immunology Virginia, LLC (Step-Down Subsidiary), adding three centres in Virginia; the Company intends to establish behaviour therapy support services at those centres over the next three years and to expand into the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom through Group Companies Carving Futures SPV Limited and Carving Futures UK Private Limited.
Attracting and retaining clinical professionals through training and upskilling: seven new 'Upskilling Academies' proposed to be set up from the Objects of the Issue.

Continuance of R&D and integration of modern technology: six 'Centres of Excellence and Research' (COER) proposed from the Issue proceeds, and stated intent to integrate AI/ML and predictive modelling into therapy services using data collected from interventions, assessments and consultations.

Continue to improve the service portfolio and build on value leadership: new offerings, improved intervention plans and cross-sell at affordable price points, including leveraging different regional programs.

Continue to grow brand awareness and brand loyalty for the 'Mom's Belief' brand through digital and conventional marketing, ATL and BTL activity and the network of Licensed Professionals and other healthcare providers.

Referral channels from partnerships: 'Company Learning Centres in partnership with Licensed Professionals' and School Collaboration Centres, under which partner professionals and schools identify and refer children, building a wide client base with reduced upfront investment.

Community and public-health outreach as a demand channel: large-scale training programs for frontline ASHA and ANM workers to strengthen early identification of neurodivergent children, plus CME programs for pediatricians and child health professionals.
strengths: Stated rank: based on number of centres as of March 31, 2026 the Company ranks first (1st) in India in offering intervention plans for children with NDDs and seventh (7th) globally among listed players in a similar behavioural health domain (Source: CARE Report, page 64).

Pan-India presence and geographic penetration: scaled from 71 centres in Fiscal 2023 to 136 centres as of March 31, 2026 (excluding three centres acquired in the US), spread across 57 cities in 20 states and union territories; 42 Tier 1, 77 Tier 2 and 17 Tier 3 centres, with presence predominantly in Tier 2 cities.

Proven track record of organic growth and scalable operations: Revenue from Operations rose from Rs 306.08 million in Fiscal 2024 to Rs 816.62 million in Fiscal 2026, a stated CAGR of 63.34%; EBITDA improved from Rs 14.91 million to Rs 119.11 million over the same period, described as a turnaround to profitability.

Asset-light centre model: all centres operate on leased premises or in schools the Company collaborates with, which the RHP states allows new-centre rollout with optimal upfront investment, limited capital expenditure and high scalability; centre-level RoCE of 4.58% in Fiscal 2024, 7.49% in Fiscal 2025 and 29.74% in Fiscal 2026.

Focus on accessibility and affordability: centres deliberately located across Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and inside partner schools, supplemented by online programs and e-therapy for those unable to visit physically; an insurance plan launched in February 2022 covering hospitalisation and online, offline and home therapies, availed by families of 429 enrolled children as of March 31, 2026.

Comprehensive, multidisciplinary, client-focused care: each enrolled child receives a personalised Individualized Education Plan (IEP) and Individualized Goal Plan (IGP), supported by occupational therapy, speech-language therapy and ABA-based behavioural support, tracked via family-shared videos and images and reviewed by clinicians.

Professional clinical team: over 340 full-time clinical professionals as of March 31, 2026, including 74 developmental and clinical psychologists, 139 occupational therapists, 72 speech-language pathologists and 50 special educators; centres equipped with 150+ teaching tools and home-based learning kits with 2,000+ teaching tools.

R&D-focused approach and digital adaptability: a seven-employee internal R&D function, two research reports published in an international journal, programmes built on evidence-based practices including PACT and JASPER, and e-therapy delivery that reached children across 13 countries besides India during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Professional and experienced management team: Promoter and Managing Director Nitin Bindlish has over 12 years of management experience in the healthcare industry and was honoured as Social Entrepreneur of the Year 2023 and featured in the 'BW 40 under 40' list.

Brand recognition built over seven years: named among the most valued mother and child brands by the Times of India in 2020 and awarded the Innovative Practice Award, 2019 by the Zero Project at the United Nations, Vienna.
threats: Risk Factor 20: low public awareness, a limited target age group (services primarily cater to children from 18 months to 12 years, with specialised programs up to age 15) and social stigma associated with NDDs may restrict demand and limit growth.

Risk Factor 24: absence of listed industry peers may affect investor benchmarking and valuation - investors must rely on their own examination of the Company's accounting ratios, Non-GAAP Measures and key performance indicators, and the absence of comparable peers may also affect the valuation of the Company and investor perception of its growth potential.
Risk Factor 25: the Company may be unable to adapt to reforms and developments in the industry, and the uncertainty associated with such reforms could adversely affect pricing and demand.

Risk Factor 5: the Company operates in a highly specialized and sensitive domain providing care to children with Neurodevelopmental Disorders, exposing it to heightened reputational, clinical and regulatory sensitivity.

Risk Factors 14 and 27: compliance obligations under applicable statutes, including the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, which is in effect in specified Notified Areas, with permits and approvals valid only for limited periods and requiring periodic renewal.
Risk Factors 32 and 33: a cyber-security breach or disruption of information technology systems could adversely affect operations - material given the paediatric clinical data handled.

Risk Factor 36: potential infringement of the Company's intellectual property and passing off by third parties using similar trade names, which could cause client confusion and a decrease in market share.
Risk Factor 44: outbreaks of diseases may adversely affect business, operations and future financial performance.
Risk Factors 55 and 56: political, economic and other factors beyond the Company's control, and changing laws, rules, regulations and legal uncertainties including adverse application of tax laws.

Competition from larger global operators noted by the CARE Report: the identified global (primarily US-listed) behavioural health companies operate at a much larger scale in terms of revenue and vertical integration, though the RHP states they are not directly comparable and cannot be considered a peer set.

Unlisted domestic operators, including NGOs, offer similar services but detailed information is largely unavailable in the public domain, so competitive intensity in the unorganised space cannot be assessed from this document.
weaknesses: Risk Factor 10: the Company has faced losses in the past and may incur losses in the future; PAT was negative at Rs (84.56) million in Fiscal 2023 with an EBITDA margin of (32.61)%.

Risk Factor 4: the Registered Office, Corporate Office, 91 of 136 centres in India and the newly acquired US centres are on premises not owned by the Company, held only under leasehold rights with staggered expiries (leases of 11 months to 3 years).
Risk Factor 11: new centres typically take 8-12 months to achieve breakeven, which could result in continued negative cash flows during the expansion phase.

Risk Factors 12 and 28: the business is highly dependent on recruiting, training and retaining specialised clinical professionals, whose number in the market is stated to be limited, and the RHP cannot assure that attrition rates will fall despite measures taken.

Risk Factor 17: previously implemented centre business models have been discontinued - all centre closures (2 in Fiscal 2026, 8 in Fiscal 2025 and 20 in Fiscal 2024) were 'Network Centres' shut following a change in Company strategy.
Risk Factor 22: the 'Upskilling Academy' initiative generates no direct revenue from operations and may continue to operate as a cost centre, which could adversely affect margins.

Risk Factor 23: none of the directors of the Company possess formal qualifications or specialized expertise directly related to the specific business activities and industry in which the Company operates.
Risk Factor 30: the degree certificates evidencing the educational qualifications of certain Key Managerial Personnel are not traceable.
Risk Factor 26: the Company has been delayed in paying certain statutory dues in the past.

Risk Factor 34: the surge in enrolments through the digital mode during the COVID-19 pandemic has since declined significantly; revenue from online services fell from Rs 11.85 million in Fiscal 2023 to Rs 3.93 million in Fiscal 2026.

Risk Factor 29: Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information included in the RHP is stated not to be indicative of future financial condition or results of operations; Fiscal 2026 is consolidated while Fiscals 2025 and 2024 are standalone, limiting like-for-like comparison.
Risk Factor 53: all industry data relied on comes from an industry report prepared by CARE which the Company commissioned and paid for solely for the purposes of the Issue.

Revenue concentration in newly acquired overseas operations: Revenue from Overseas Centres of Rs 340.85 million in Fiscal 2026 against Nil in each of Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, i.e. a large share of Fiscal 2026 growth has no operating history under Company ownership.

overview.business_model: The Company earns fees from delivering early-intervention and therapy programmes for children with neurodevelopmental disorders through a diversified network of centres: Company Learning Centres (wholly established and managed by the Company), Company Learning Centres in partnership with Licensed Professionals, School Collaboration Centres embedded within educational institutions, Centres for Excellence and Research (COER), and an in-house Upskilling Academy. Services blend in-person therapy at centres with digital/virtual consultations and home-delivered customised learning kits, plus a library of over 2,000 teaching tools that trains parents as co-therapists. Revenue from Operations for Fiscal 2026 was Rs 816.62 million (consolidated), split as domestic centre operations Rs 261.68 million (32.04%), online services Rs 3.93 million (0.48%), other operating revenue Rs 1.44 million (0.18%), export of services Rs 208.72 million (25.56%) and overseas centres Rs 340.85 million (41.74%). Export services comprise R&D and clinical innovation support provided to the Holding Company and business support services (accounting, HR, digital marketing, data management) to a Promoter Group entity. The Company operated 136 centres in India across 57 cities and 20 states/union territories as of March 31, 2026 (139 total centres per its operational KPI table).

concerns_observed: The three-year series is not like-for-like and the headline jump is not organic: FY2026 is restated CONSOLIDATED (Mom's Belief US Inc. acquired June 23, 2025) while FY2025 and FY2024 are restated STANDALONE. Overseas-centre revenue of Rs 340.85 million is 41.74% of FY2026 revenue and nil in both prior years, so the move from Rs 364.19 million to Rs 816.62 million is predominantly acquisition-driven, not centre growth.

A quarter of revenue is billed to the controlling shareholder and its affiliate, and most of it is unpaid: export of services was Rs 208.72 million (25.56% of FY2026 revenue) - Rs 148.25 million to Holding Company and 91.43% Corporate Promoter Carving Futures Pte. Ltd. and Rs 60.47 million to promoter-group entity Carving Futures, Inc. - while Rs 112.91 million of the Rs 180.88 million total trade receivables at March 31, 2026 was owed by those same two related parties.

Operating cash flow is negative in two of three years and receivables have blown out: CFO was Rs (19.41) million in FY2026 and Rs (18.11) million in FY2025 against reported PAT of Rs 49.59 million and Rs 58.81 million; FY2026 working capital absorbed Rs (142.90) million, chiefly a Rs (108.30) million rise in trade receivables, and receivable days went 2 (FY2024) to 31 (FY2025) to 81 (FY2026).

FY2025 PAT of Rs 58.81 million exceeds FY2026 PAT of Rs 49.59 million only because of a one-time non-cash deferred tax credit of Rs 55.33 million - the RHP itself states that without it FY2025 PAT would have been Rs 3.48 million. Any three-year PAT trend read off the headline line is misleading in both directions.

Two of the five objects pay rent, not growth: Rs 144.45 million funds lease payments on the 136 EXISTING India centres for Fiscals 2027-2029 and Rs 101.31 million is invested into Mom's Belief US Inc. to pay lease/licence on the three EXISTING Virginia centres - recurring operating cost of the current business funded from primary issue proceeds.

Zero committed capex against a Rs 413.61 million capex object: the RHP states 'As of now, there are no orders placed', no definitive vendor agreements and no lease arrangements for any of the 319 New Centres, whose exact locations are not yet identified. Every fit-out and therapy-material quotation is dated August 12-13, 2026 and 'valid for a period of 12 months', lapsing around August 2027 - while Rs 199.65 million of the capex object falls in Fiscal 2028 and a further Rs 100.11 million in Fiscal 2029, entirely after that expiry.

The rollout being funded is 2.3x the existing estate (136 to 455 centres) but actual new-centre capex collapsed in the year immediately before the ask: Rs 1.31 million on 8,350 sq ft in FY2026 against Rs 19.49 million on 49,518 sq ft in FY2025 and Rs 12.76 million on 30,177 sq ft in FY2024; new centres take 8-12 months to reach breakeven per Risk Factor 11.

Object 5 - funding inorganic growth through an unidentified acquisition plus general corporate purposes - is printed as '[.]' in every column with no definitive agreement in place, subject only to the 25% GCP cap and the 35% combined cap on the amount raised.

Two of the Company's own centre models have already been abandoned: 45 centres were closed across FY2024-FY2026 (20, 8 and 2), all of them 'Network Centres' launched in Fiscal 2019 and first discontinued in Fiscal 2021; and the August 2024 joint venture that started with 9 pilot centres was taken over and discontinued in March 2025.

Throughput has not grown with the estate: children served were 9,344 (FY2024), 8,585 (FY2025) and 9,205 (FY2026) - FY2026 still below FY2024 - while India centres nearly doubled from 71 to 136, so domestic revenue growth is not being carried by volume.

People risk is the cost base: 229 of 521 permanent employees resigned in FY2026 (against 148 and 149 in the prior two years), average monthly attrition of clinical professionals was 4.41% in FY2026, and employee benefit expense was Rs 394.46 million, 52.48% of total expenses of Rs 751.61 million.

The Company carries only group health insurance for employees and holds NO insurance for fire, theft, natural disasters, terrorism or cyber-security breach (Risk Factor 47) - across 136 leased premises where children with disabilities receive in-person therapy.

The stated international expansion into the UAE and the UK is to be pursued 'through Group Companies Carving Futures SPV Limited and Carving Futures UK Private Limited' - promoter-side entities outside the listed company - while the RHP separately states Group Companies have no common pursuits with the Company.

Two revenue lines the RHP promotes are not earning: online services fell from Rs 11.85 million in Fiscal 2023 to Rs 3.93 million in FY2026 (0.48% of revenue, with only 233 online enrolments), and the Upskilling Academy recorded nil Revenue from Operations in all three Fiscals while Rs 20.45 million of proceeds is earmarked for five more of them.

The issue is managed by a single BRLM, Mefcom Capital Markets Limited, and Risk Factor 72 discloses that the current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous IPOs managed by that BRLM is below their respective issue prices.

What is the composition and margin of the Rs 340.85 million of Overseas Centre revenue? The acquired Virginia business is an allergy, asthma and immunology medical practice - not NDD intervention - and the RHP prints its revenue from external customers but no separate segment profitability, nor any indication of Medicaid or US payor dependence.

Why did actual capex on new centres fall to Rs 1.31 million on 8,350 sq ft in FY2026 from Rs 19.49 million on 49,518 sq ft in FY2025, in the year immediately preceding a Rs 413.61 million capex ask covering 319 new centres?

Children served fell to 9,205 in FY2026 from 9,344 in FY2024 while India centres rose from 71 to 136 - is the growth in domestic centre revenue (Rs 193.25 million to Rs 261.68 million) price-led, mix-led, or driven purely by the 4,265 repeat clients, and is per-centre throughput therefore falling?

The Monitoring Agency is CARE Ratings Limited while the commissioned industry report relied on throughout the RHP is by CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited - are these within the same group, and if so does that bear on the independence of Regulation 41 utilisation monitoring?
Why did the statutory auditor change three times in three years, with two resignations (P Chopra & Co., September 02, 2023; SBRK & Co., June 04, 2024) for which the RHP states no reason?

Five senior people left in the eighteen months to July 2026 - Country Head Ravi Shekhar (January 31, 2026), Business Head Rajesh MS (April 30, 2026), GM Revenue Manish Verma (June 27, 2026, appointed only January 12, 2026), and Executive Directors Rajeev and Mohd Naushad (both July 24, 2025) - with no reason stated for any, against the RHP's assertion that KMP/SMP attrition 'is not high'.

What happens to the Rs 216.53 million (26.52% of FY2026 revenue) earned through 104 partnership centres when non-compete and non-solicitation clauses expire? They run only 24 months within a radius of up to 5 kilometres, after which the Licensed Professional may open a competing centre nearby and solicit both clients and clinical staff.
verdict.our_read: Rays of Belief runs 136 leased 'Mom's Belief' centres across 57 Indian cities delivering therapy for children with neurodevelopmental disorders, but only 32.04% of its Fiscal 2026 Revenue from Operations of Rs 816.62 million (Rs 81.66 crore) came from those Indian centres - 41.74% came from a Virginia allergy, asthma and immunology practice acquired on June 23, 2025 and 25.56% from support-service exports billed to its own Singapore holding company and a promoter-group entity - so the make-or-break question is whether the domestic NDD business, which grew only Rs 193.25 million to Rs 261.68 million over three Fiscals, can carry the 319-centre, Rs 413.61 million expansion this Issue is meant to fund.

parameter_scores.asset_and_lease_risk: Elevated. The Company owns no immovable property; 91 of 136 India centres are leased on 11-month to 3-year tenures with 5-10% escalations and renewals conditioned on hikes up to 20%, and 30-37% of Company Learning Centre capex is immovable fit-out that is written off on exit.
parameter_scores.audit_estimate_dependence: High. Two of three Key Audit Matters - a Rs 55.05 million deferred tax asset on management profit projections and Rs 49.92 million of provisional goodwill with USD 0.90 million contingent consideration valued by management without an independent valuation - rest on unverified internal estimates, though the audit opinion is unmodified.
parameter_scores.balance_sheet_strength: Strong on the face of it. Rs 36.07 million of borrowing against Rs 308.10 million of equity (printed D/E 0.12, DSCR 11.11 times), Rs 32.55 million of cash, zero pledge, nil contingent liabilities and nil capital commitments as affirmatively stated.
parameter_scores.capital_structure_hygiene: Aggressive pre-Issue. A 45-for-1 bonus on June 19, 2025 produced 95.7% of pre-Issue capital within 18 months of the RHP; secondary WACA is Rs 0.22 against Pre-IPO placements at Rs 284-290 nine months later. Offsetting this: pure Fresh Issue, no OFS, no promoter selling.
parameter_scores.cash_conversion: Poor. CFO was Rs (19.41) million in FY2026 and Rs (18.11) million in FY2025; receivable days moved 2 to 31 to 81, and FY2026 working capital absorbed Rs (142.90) million of which Rs (108.30) million was the receivables build.
parameter_scores.disclosure_consistency: Below par. At least six internal contradictions across strike-off dates, pending registration counts, a director's independence designation, centre counts, clinical headcount and a related-party advance figure.
parameter_scores.earnings_quality: Distorted across the series. FY2025 PAT of Rs 58.81 million rests on a Rs 55.33 million non-cash deferred tax credit against PBT of Rs 3.48 million; FY2024 PAT of Rs 8.53 million similarly benefits from a Rs 7.53 million deferred tax credit on PBT of Rs 1.00 million. Only FY2026 (PBT Rs 69.03 million, PAT Rs 49.59 million) is operationally earned.
parameter_scores.governance_depth: Thin. No director holds any qualification relevant to the business; 3 of 5 directors are independent but all were appointed between April and May 2025; three auditor changes in three years; both finance KMPs' degree certificates untraceable; five senior departures in eighteen months with no reasons stated.
parameter_scores.growth_organic_vs_acquired: Predominantly acquired. Revenue Rs 364.19 million to Rs 816.62 million is mostly the Rs 340.85 million of overseas-centre revenue that was nil in both prior years; the organic domestic centre line moved Rs 213.09 million to Rs 261.68 million.
parameter_scores.insurance_and_operational_cover: Materially inadequate. Only group health insurance for employees; no cover for fire, theft, natural disaster, terrorism or cyber breach across 136 leased premises where children with disabilities are treated in person.
parameter_scores.litigation_exposure: Clean as disclosed. Nil against the Company, Subsidiaries, Directors, KMP, Senior Management and Promoters, and nil SEBI or exchange action against Promoters in five Fiscals; the three live matters were filed by the Company, claiming Rs 24.50 million.
parameter_scores.model_stability: Unproven. Two centre models have already been abandoned - Network Centres (45 closed over FY2024-26) and the August 2024 joint venture (9 pilot centres absorbed and shut in March 2025) - and 104 of 136 centres depend on Licensed Professionals whose non-competes run only 24 months within 5 kilometres.
parameter_scores.objects_readiness: Low. Zero orders placed on the entire Rs 413.61 million capex object, no vendor or lease agreements signed, New Centre locations not identified, and quotations dated August 12-13, 2026 lapse around August 2027 while Rs 199.65 million of deployment sits in FY2028 and Rs 100.11 million in FY2029. Only the two lease objects (Rs 144.45 million and Rs 101.31 million) rest on executed contracts.
parameter_scores.peer_benchmarking: Impossible by the issuer's own disclosure, not by omission. The RHP states four times that no comparable listed company exists in India or any foreign jurisdiction; the six global names in the commissioned CARE report (Acadia, LifeStance, UHS, BrightSpring, Addus, Humana) are expressly stated not to be a peer set and carry no P/E, RoNW, NAV or EPS.
parameter_scores.people_dependency: High. 229 of 521 permanent employees resigned in FY2026; clinical professional attrition averaged 4.41% monthly; employee cost was Rs 394.46 million, 52.48% of total expenses.
parameter_scores.regulatory_compliance: Patchy but self-disclosed. SEBI SBEB non-compliance on the SAR Scheme (ordinary rather than special resolution, rescinded August 05, 2025), eight late statutory-dues instances of 1-18 days, delayed DPT-3/MSME-1/MGT-14/BEN-2 filings, and CERR registrations still pending across seven states.
parameter_scores.related_party_exposure: High and structural. 25.56% of FY2026 revenue and Rs 112.91 million of Rs 180.88 million total receivables sit with the Corporate Promoter (91.43% holder) and a promoter-group entity, with no pricing mechanism disclosed.
parameter_scores.revenue_quality: Weak. Only 32.04% of FY2026 revenue came from the Indian centre business the Company is actually built on; 25.56% was billed to its own Holding Company and a promoter-group entity, and 41.74% came from a US practice owned for nine months of the year.
parameter_scores.unit_economics_visibility: Low. No centre-level utilisation, no customer concentration, no B2B/B2C revenue split and no overseas segment profitability; children served (9,205 in FY2026) is still below FY2024's 9,344 despite the estate rising from 71 to 136 centres.
parameter_scores.use_of_proceeds_quality: Mixed. Rs 245.76 million of the quantified objects funds rent on already-operating India and US centres rather than growth, and Object 5 (unidentified acquisition plus GCP, capped at 35% of the amount raised) is entirely unquantified.
parameter_scores.valuation_assessability: Not assessable. No Price Band is fixed; P/E and market-cap-to-revenue are printed as '[.]' placeholders, and the issuer itself states four separate times that no listed company in India or any foreign jurisdiction is comparable, so no relative benchmark exists either. Printed facts only: Pre-IPO Placements at Rs 284 and Rs 290 per share, WACA of Rs 225.59 (primary) and Rs 0.22 (secondary), NAV per share Rs 15.67, EPS Rs 3.21.

red_flags: The fastest-growing revenue line is billed to the controlling shareholder and is largely uncollected: export of services to Carving Futures Pte. Ltd. (which holds 91.43% of the Company and is also its Holding Company) rose Rs 104.44 million to Rs 123.07 million to Rs 148.25 million across FY2024-FY2026, and services to Carving Futures, Inc. went from nil to Rs 21.31 million to Rs 60.47 million - yet Rs 64.30 million and Rs 48.61 million respectively were still outstanding as trade receivables at March 31, 2026. The RHP prints no pricing mechanism or benchmark for these intra-group service agreements.

A 45-for-1 bonus on June 19, 2025 created 14,994,540 of the 15,671,682 pre-Issue shares - 95.7% of pre-Issue capital - within the 18 months preceding this RHP; the disclosed weighted average cost of acquisition is Rs 225.59 for the last five primary transactions and Rs 0.22 for secondary transactions, against Pre-IPO Placements completed nine to eleven months later at Rs 284 and Rs 290 per share.

Two of the three Key Audit Matters rest on management's own unverified estimates with an unmodified opinion: a Rs 55.05 million deferred tax asset recognised at FY2026 on management projections of future taxable profit against carried-forward business losses of Rs 171.93 million and unabsorbed depreciation of Rs 9.01 million; and PROVISIONAL goodwill of Rs 49.92 million on the Mom's Belief US Inc. acquisition, whose USD 0.90 million contingent consideration in performance-linked stock options was measured at management's own estimate with no independent valuation.

Disclosed SEBI non-compliance: the Stock Appreciation Rights Scheme was adopted by ORDINARY resolution where the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 mandate a SPECIAL resolution. The scheme was rescinded on August 05, 2025 with no benefits availed, but the RHP states there is no assurance SEBI or another regulator will not take adverse action for the past non-compliance.

The statutory auditor changed three times in the three years preceding this RHP - P Chopra & Co. resigned September 02, 2023; SBRK & Co. resigned June 04, 2024; V. P. Batra & Co.'s term completed September 30, 2024; Suri & Sudhir appointed September 30, 2024 - and no reason is printed for any of the resignations.

The RHP contradicts itself in at least six places: Crafting Futures Private Limited's strike-off is dated 'May 06, 2025' in Note 40 and 'May 06, 2026' on p.79; Shops and Establishments registrations pending are 2 centres (Risk Factor 14) versus 3 centres in Karnataka, Sikkim and J&K (Government and Other Approvals); Afzal Mohammed Modak is designated 'Independent Director' in the IPO Committee table but Non-Executive and Non-Independent everywhere else; the centre count is 136 in the business chapter and 139 in the operational KPI table; advances to Carving Futures Inc for FY2025 print as '-' in Note 40 and 0.01 in the summary; and clinical professionals are '337' in Risk Factor 12 and 340 elsewhere.

Neither of the two finance-side KMPs can produce their qualifying certificates: Ved Prakash (CFO) and Mayank Bhargava (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer) have both been unable to trace their bachelor's degree certificates in commerce, with reliance placed on mark sheets and self-executed affidavits pending university responses.

No director on the five-member Board holds any formal qualification or specialised expertise related to the Company's business - the RHP states verbatim that none have 'obtained formal training or qualifications (clinically) held positions that are directly aligned with the technical or operational aspects of our business sector' - in a company delivering clinical intervention to children with disabilities.

Regulatory registrations for the actual clinical estate are incomplete: CERR registrations applied for but not obtained for centres in Uttar Pradesh, Sikkim, Telangana, West Bengal, Rajasthan, Bihar and Jharkhand, plus pending Shops and Establishments registrations, a pending Sikkim professional tax registration and pending GST certificate updations across seven states; the affected centres contributed Rs 3.90 million (0.48% of revenue) in FY2026.

Statutory dues were repeatedly deposited late - eight disclosed instances across ESIC, EPF, GST and TDS with delays of 1 to 18 days (the TDS due May 7, 2023 filed May 15, 2023; supplementary ESIC due September 15, 2025 filed October 03, 2025) - alongside delayed RoC filings of forms DPT-3, MSME-1, MGT-14 and BEN-2 regularised only on payment of late fees.
strengths_observed: The domestic centre business grew without the acquisition: revenue from India centre operations rose Rs 193.25 million (FY2024) to Rs 213.09 million (FY2025) to Rs 261.68 million (FY2026), with the centre count going 71 to 111 to 136 and disclosed centre RoCE improving 4.58% to 7.49% to 29.74% across the same three Fiscals.

Repeat engagement improved materially: clients with more than 12 sessions were 2,694 (FY2024), 2,524 (FY2025) and 4,265 (FY2026), while fresh enrolments were roughly flat at 7,307 / 6,512 / 6,903 - so FY2026 growth came from families staying longer rather than from acquiring more of them.

Balance sheet is close to unlevered and unencumbered: total borrowing of Rs 36.07 million (a single unsecured inter-corporate loan at 14%) against net worth of Rs 308.10 million, printed Debt-Equity of 0.12 and Debt Service Coverage of 11.11 times; zero promoter shares pledged, and the issuer affirmatively states nil contingent liabilities and nil capital commitments for FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024.

EBITDA turned from a Rs 84.56 million loss in Fiscal 2023 to Rs 14.91 million (4.87%) in FY2024, Rs 30.17 million (8.28%) in FY2025 and Rs 119.11 million (14.59%) in FY2026, and the issuer's EBITDA definition reconciles to the printed PBT, finance cost, depreciation and other-income lines in each of the three years.

This is a pure Fresh Issue of up to 5,230,000 Equity Shares with 'Offer for Sale Size: Not applicable' - no promoter, no Rainmatter, no KAPICO and no pre-IPO investor is selling a single share, and the Rs 58.95 million of Pre-IPO Placements has already been reduced from the Fresh Issue size.

Litigation position as disclosed is clean: nil proceedings against the Company, Subsidiaries, Directors, KMP, Senior Management or Promoters, nil SEBI or stock-exchange disciplinary action against the Promoters in five Fiscals; the only three matters are brought BY the Company (a 2022 data-theft complaint against an ex-employee plus two civil suits claiming Rs 24.50 million).

CARE Ratings Limited was appointed Monitoring Agency under Regulation 41 (agreement dated August 14, 2026) with quarterly reporting to the Audit Committee until Gross Proceeds and Net Pre-IPO Proceeds are fully utilised - relevant given Object 5 is an unquantified acquisition and general-corporate bucket.

Clinical bench is real and specified: 340 full-time clinical professionals as of March 31, 2026 - 74 developmental and clinical psychologists, 139 occupational therapists, 72 speech-language pathologists and 50 special educators - within 521 permanent employees and 19 consultants.

The two lease objects are the only contract-backed uses of proceeds: Rs 144.45 million for existing India centre leases and Rs 101.31 million for the three US centres are stated to rest on 'valid and existing lease agreements and leave and license agreements which have been executed', unlike the capex object.

Cost estimates carry two independent certifications - Ar. Tracy Kikon, Independent Architect (certificate dated February 11, 2026) for all fit-out costs, and Suri and Sudhir, Chartered Accountants (certificate dated August 18, 2026) for the Upskilling Academy, hardware, US lease, brand and GCP objects.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light service model with no manufacturing and no backward or forward integration disclosed. The DRHP states affirmatively that 'Our Company is not in the business of manufacturing and therefore, the Company has not undertaken any steps for capacity/facility creation' (PDF p.255), and that 'We do not own any immovable property' - the Registered Office, Corporate Office and all 136 India centres operate from leased or rented premises, or from premises provided by Licensed Professionals and partner schools, on lease tenures of 11 months to 3 years (Our Business - Properties, PDF p.241). Upstream inputs are limited to centre fit-outs (interior, electrical, furniture, branding), initial inventory of therapy material and technology hardware (printers, laptops), all procured against quotations from third-party contractors and vendors and certified by an Independent Architect (Objects of the Issue, PDF p.117-118); immovable fit-out capex is approximately 30-37% of total centre capex for Company Learning Centres and partnership centres and under 9% for School Collaboration Centres, and is not recoverable if a lease ends (Risk Factor 1). Forward reach is through owned centre formats plus revenue-share partnerships with Licensed Professionals (who provide premises and referrals) and with schools, complemented by e-therapy delivered digitally and home-delivered learning kits built on an in-house library of 2,000+ teaching tools developed by a seven-person R&D team. The Company also runs an in-house Upskilling Academy for clinician training and a Centre for Excellence and Research. ABSENCES, ATTRIBUTED: the DRHP discloses NO order book, order-in-hand or unexecuted-contract value anywhere (searched the full document for 'order book', 'orders in hand', 'unexecuted' - zero hits); NO top-1/top-5/top-10 customer concentration table and NO supplier or vendor concentration table are printed in any section (Business, Risk Factors, Other Financial Information or MD&A); and NO B2B versus B2C revenue split percentage is printed - the only B2B/B2C distinction in the document is in the expected-credit-loss note, where trade receivables as at March 31, 2026 are split as B2C Rs 1.58 million and corporate/B2B Rs 113.16 million (standalone) plus Mom's Belief US Inc. Rs 68.66 million, which is a receivables ageing, not a revenue mix. NOTE ON BASIS: the domestic_export_mix percentages above are on a '% of total income' basis (MD&A Results of Operations table, PDF p.368) - the only basis on which the DRHP prints a consolidated domestic percentage. risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- A quarter of revenue rests on agreements with entities the Promoter controls, so it is neither arm's-length demand nor independently renewable; the DRHP also flags 50.21% of Fiscal 2025 Pro Forma Revenue from Operations on the same basis, and the receivables against these services are what turned operating cash flow negative
- All 136 India centres, the Registered Office, the Corporate Office and the US centres are leased (91 of 136 India centres are in premises not owned by the Company); a landlord refusing renewal strands the fit-out spend, and the entire Rs 413.61 million New Centre capex plan is fit-out on someone else's property
- These practitioners are independent, supply the physical space and control the referral funnel; termination or a lapse in coordination removes both the client pipeline and the location at once
- The Company plans to more than treble its network in three years while every added centre carries costs before revenue; the Company already reports time and cost overruns in setting up centres, has had negative operating cash flow in Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026, and the funding plan is not appraised by any bank or independent agency
- Over 340 full-time clinical professionals as of March 31, 2026 with average monthly attrition of 4.41% for clinical staff; the specialist NDD pool is thin, thinnest in the Tier 3 cities the expansion targets, and inability to staff a centre forces service curtailment or costly relocation
- Mom's Belief US, Inc. and Allergy & Immunology Virginia, LLC were acquired only on June 23, 2025 and operate an allergy/asthma/immunology practice rather than the core NDD business; the Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information for Fiscal 2025 is illustrative only and Fiscal 2026 consolidated numbers are not comparable to the prior standalone years
- Diagnosis and enrolment depend on families overcoming stigma and misconceptions, particularly in semi-urban and rural India; low enrolment, mid-programme discontinuation and payment constraints directly hit centre utilisation and revenue
- The DRHP states there are no listed Indian peers in a directly comparable business, so investors cannot benchmark the Issue Price; separately, none of the directors hold formal clinical qualifications or specialised expertise in the Company's field, leaving clinical oversight to Clinical/Medical Directors below Board level
